transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I'm here because... well, work has been a little difficult lately. I keep, um, getting up during our long sales strategy meetings. I know I'm supposed to stay seated, but I just end up finding reasons to leave... like getting water or just pacing by the printer.
When you're not at work—like at home in the evenings or on weekends—do you notice the same difficulty sitting still, or is this mainly something that happens during those meetings at work?

I mean... maybe a little at home. But work is mostly why I'm bringing it up. It's... well, it's starting to show up in my performance reviews. And, um... with client trust. There was a specific client complaint recently that... I don't know, it just really made me worry I might damage my accounts. I really do care about doing good work, it's just... yeah. Work is where it's a problem right now.

Going back to when you were a child or teenager in school, did you have similar trouble sitting still in class, or is this difficulty something that's mostly started happening more recently as an adult?

Um... no, it's not really a new thing. It goes back... way before high school, actually. 

I guess... well, in elementary school, my teachers used to leave notes about it. They'd write that I was bright, but that I rushed through things. And, um... that I talked out of turn. I'd forget my homework a lot. My desk was always just stuffed with half-finished papers. So... yeah. It's not just starting now.
Over the past 6 months or so, would you say these difficulties with sitting still, rushing through things, and staying organized have been pretty much constant, or do they come and go?

Um... I guess they're pretty constant. They don't really come and go. 

It's... well, it's been noticeably affecting me since I changed into advertising sales strategy. That was about two years and two months ago. So... yeah. It's been constant since then.
When you're working on a task or project, do you find it hard to keep your attention on it until it's finished, or do you tend to move on to something else before completing it?

Um... yeah, I suppose so. Like... if I'm reading a client brief, or in one of those longer strategy meetings... I usually start out focused enough. But... after a few minutes, I'll realize I've just been staring at the exact same slide. Or the same paragraph. And I... I just have no idea what the last point even was. So... yeah.
When you think back to elementary school, around what age do you think these difficulties—the trouble sitting still, rushing through things, and losing focus—first started to show up?

Um... I'm not really sure about an exact age. It's hard to remember. I just... I know it was early on. Like I said, those notes from teachers were in elementary school. But... I don't know exactly how old I was when it started.
When you think about first grade or second grade specifically, do you remember having trouble paying attention or sitting still even back then?

Um... yeah, I guess so. I mean... it was definitely before high school. I just remember my teachers back then... they'd write on my report cards that I was smart, but that I rushed through everything. And... that I talked when I wasn't supposed to. Or forgot my homework. My desk was always just... full of papers I never finished. So... yeah, I guess it was happening back then, too.
When you're sitting down—like at your desk or in a meeting—do you find yourself fidgeting with things, bouncing your leg, or feeling restless in your body, or is it more just that your mind wanders?
Um... I don't really notice myself doing that. I don't think I bounce my leg or anything. So... yeah, I guess it's mostly just my mind wandering.

You mentioned talking out of turn in school and leaving meetings to pace—do you find yourself talking a lot, interrupting people, or having trouble waiting your turn in conversations, even now as an adult?

Um... I guess so. Sometimes. Like, when we're doing team pitches at work... I'll realize I've been talking about a campaign idea for a while. And... um, when I finally stop, I can just sort of tell that the others were waiting for me to finish so they could say something. So, yeah... I guess I do talk a bit much sometimes.

You mentioned you get up and pace during meetings—when you do that, is it because you physically feel like you need to move around, or is it more that you just lose focus and use it as an excuse to leave?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't thought about it that much. I just... kind of find myself getting up. I don't really know if it's one or the other, to be honest.
Beyond work, how much are these difficulties with attention, sitting still, and organization affecting other parts of your life—like your relationships, hobbies, or managing things at home?

Um... I don't really know about at home. It's... fine, I guess. I mostly just notice it at work. 

Um... it's actually started showing up in my performance reviews. And... just with client trust, I guess. There was this one client complaint recently, and... well, it just made me worry that I could really damage my accounts. Even though I care a lot about doing a good job. So... yeah. I don't really know about outside of work.
